title: MATH 3042 Statistics · Quiz 8
subtitle: The next lab quiz: all of Unit 5, continuous distributions on paper and in RStudio
description: A three-hour drill shaped like the quiz, written to be read with no earlier knowledge of Unit 5: a pre-reading page for the calculator keys, how the past quizzes are written, one short lesson per idea (area as probability, uniform, the normal curve, the Z table forwards and backwards, two-step questions, exponential waits, percentiles and the memoryless fact, then the p, q and r functions in RStudio), two mock quizzes in the real two-part format, and a one-page know-cold sheet.
intro:
:::quiz Quiz 8
**In the lab session, 50 minutes.** Part 1 is paper and pencil with a calculator (10 marks); Part 2 is RStudio, knitting a notebook from the Learning Hub template to a Word file (10 marks). The scope is all of Unit 5, continuous probability distributions: uniform, normal with the Z table, exponential. A probability is rounded to four decimal places; μ, σ and Z to two. No makeups.
:::

lessons.title: A continuous variable: probability is an area, and one exact value has probability 0
Uniform on paper: a rectangle of width b − a and height 1/(b − a)
The normal curve: μ puts the centre, σ sets the width
The Z table: the area to the left of z
Any normal on paper: turn x into Z, then use the table
From a percentage back to a value: the table read backwards, then x = μ + Zσ
Two-step questions: a threshold between two levels, and a normal answer used as a binomial p
Exponential on paper: a waiting time with mean β
Exponential backwards and memoryless: solve for the time with ln; time already waited does not count
